disclaimer.section1_body: CorrelCore measures statistical correlations — patterns that appear together in your data. A correlation does not mean one thing causes the other.
disclaimer.section2_title: What does the confidence bar mean?
disclaimer.section2_body: The bar shows how consistent and reliable the pattern is, based on the number of entries and the strength of the association. More data means higher confidence.
disclaimer.section3_title: What is the minimum data requirement?
disclaimer.section3_body: CorrelCore needs at least 30 entries with both variables present to show an insight. The “Based on N entries” subtext shows the exact sample size.
disclaimer.section4_body: Depending on the data type: Spearman rank correlation (ordinal × ordinal), point-biserial correlation (binary × continuous), or Pearson r (continuous × continuous). The expanded card shows the exact method and coefficient.
disclaimer.section5_title: How should I read symptom Lift values?
disclaimer.section5_body: Lift compares how often a symptom and tag appear together with what you would expect if they were independent. Lift = 1 means no unusual overlap, Lift > 1 means they co-occur more often than expected, and Lift < 1 means less often. An asterisk (*) marks pairs that remain notable after false-discovery-rate correction.

concepts.title: Tag, habit or symptom?
concepts.intro: You attach all three to a daily entry — CorrelCore analyses them differently.
concepts.tag_body: A context label for a day — e.g. Walk, Alcohol, Meeting. No target, no schedule. CorrelCore looks at what co-occurs and how it relates to your metrics.
concepts.habit_body: A behavior you want to build or reduce — with a target frequency. CorrelCore shows your adherence over time and how it relates to your metrics. A habit is really just a tag with a goal — you can set that during onboarding or later in Settings.
concepts.symptom_body: Something you experience physically or mentally — e.g. headache, rumination. CorrelCore looks for associations with mood and energy.
concepts.cycle_body: Optional: log your cycle day (1–35). CorrelCore treats it like a metric and looks for links with mood, sleep and more. No prediction, no medical advice.
concepts.footer: Statements stay descriptive, not a diagnosis.
concepts.info_label: What do tag, habit and symptom mean?

privacy.page_subtitle: How this CorrelCore installation handles your data
privacy.intro: This policy applies to your use of this CorrelCore instance. For selfhosted deployments, the instance operator is the data controller. Full legal text is also in docs/PRIVACY.md in the repository.

controller.heading: Who is responsible?
controller.body: On a selfhosted instance, the person or organisation running the server is the controller under GDPR. CorrelCore is the software; it does not process your data on a central cloud by default.

data.heading: What data is processed?
data.body: Mood, energy, stress, symptoms, optional notes, tags, habits, and account data (email, display name). Health-related fields are encrypted at rest. No third-party ad or analytics trackers are used.

legal.heading: Legal basis
legal.body: Health diary data is processed on the basis of your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) and Art. 9(2)(a) GDPR). Account functions rely on contract performance. You can withdraw consent by disabling analysis or deleting your account.

security.heading: Security
security.body: TLS in transit, app-level encryption for sensitive fields, row-level security, rate limiting, and structured logs without plaintext health data. Backups are the operator's responsibility; encrypted restic backups are recommended.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: Access and portability: export ZIP/JSON/CSV in Settings. Erasure: delete account in Settings (password required). Object to analysis: turn off "Analysis enabled". Restriction (Art. 18): contact your instance operator — see DSGVO.md.

sharing.heading: Third parties
sharing.body: Health data is not sent to cloud LLMs, ad networks, or external analytics. Optional selfhosted error tracking (GlitchTip) must not include plaintext health fields.

retention.heading: Retention
retention.body: Entries remain until you delete them or your account. Generated insights use a rolling window. Unverified accounts may be removed after seven days.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.body: This policy is updated when processing changes materially. The in-app page and docs/PRIVACY.md in the repository are the authoritative sources for selfhost users.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Privacy requests: contact your instance operator. Security issues: see SECURITY.md in the repository.

landing.hero_title: Understand why some days are good — and others aren't.
landing.hero_subtitle: CorrelCore is a privacy-first mood & habit tracker with correlation analysis. Log 60 seconds a day; let the data explain the rest. No gamification, ever.
landing.preview_matrix: Insight matrix: associations ranked by effect size.
landing.preview_card: Insight card: one observation, stated plainly.
landing.preview_heatmap: Tag heatmap: what co-occurs, grouped by cluster.
landing.android_body: A signed APK straight from GitHub Releases. Subscribe to the repo with Obtainium to get updates automatically — no app store required.
landing.android_sha256: Every release ships SHA256SUMS.txt so you can verify the download.

1.title: Correlations, not raw data
1.body: Statistical analysis surfaces which factors — sleep, exercise, remote-work days — actually relate to your mood and energy.

2.title: 60 seconds a day
2.body: Mood, energy, stress, tags and symptoms — quick enough to keep doing, not another chore.

3.title: No gamification, ever
3.body: No performance pressure, no artificial urgency. Just tracking consistency, for your own reflection.

landing.viz_correlations: Insight matrix, insight card, and tag heatmap (product preview)
landing.selfhost_body: CorrelCore runs on your own server — a NAS, a VPS, a spare machine. No account with us, no telemetry, no third-party analytics. One command gets you a running instance.
landing.tech_body: FastAPI + PostgreSQL backend, SvelteKit web frontend. No hidden logic — read the source, self-host it, or contribute.

1.a: No. CorrelCore is not a medical diagnostic tool. All insights are for personal reflection only — they show associations, not causes.

2.q: Do I need to self-host it?
2.a: Yes, for now — CorrelCore is a self-hosted release. Docker Compose brings up the full stack in minutes; offline-capable mobile support is planned.

3.q: What if I only have a few days of data?
3.a: Insights are labeled by confidence — "Early pattern" through "Robust" — so you always know how much to trust a correlation yet.
